workflowRecommendation: One implementer, tasks in order 0-8. Tasks 1-4 are one behaviour commit (environment.ts + consumers + tests); Task 5 docs and Task 6 smoke are their own commits and can be written while the Task 6 rig run is in progress; Task 7 is a separable commit the architect may cut. Skip formatters/linters/project-wide tests until the end (biome + tsc + `bun test packages/daemon` once before pushing). The tester repeats Task 6's environ command on a rig pane and adds the negative control (a production pane on the old daemon showing 2).
spec: dispatch_doc_read LEGION-74 (spec v2): acceptance 1-7, Requirements, Design, Errors, Testing, Rejected. The plan argues from it; read both.
goal: Every Legion pane (root architect, phase worker, controller), the private tmux server that hosts them, both start-up OMP probes, and every daemon child that runs through createDaemonRunner inherit an explicit allow-list of the daemon's environment plus the complete `mise env` output - never the two GitHub App private keys, provider keys, Dispatch/Envoy secrets, or anything else the daemon alone should hold. The daemon still reads the keys for its own token minting.

designSummary.oneChange: `resolveDaemonEnvironment` (environment.ts) builds `paneEnv` with `paneEnvironment(daemonEnv, miseEnv)`: pick(PANE_ENV_ALLOW_LIST) from the daemon's environment, lay the whole `mise env --json` output over it, drop credential-shaped names (`isSecretLikeName`). `paneEnv` is already what `createDaemonRunner` gives every jj/git/gh/tmux/probe command, what the private tmux server is forked with, and therefore what every pane inherits beneath its explicit `-e` pairs - so `processes.ts`, `runtime-tmux.ts`, and `boot-probes.ts` need no code change (verified: processes.ts only consumes `processPath`; runtime-tmux.ts:200-211 adds `-e` pairs; boot-probes.ts:167-176 passes no env; fetch.ts:81-83 hands `options.env` to Bun.spawn verbatim).

threeEnvironmentClasses.paneEnv (allow-list + mise, credential-s: every pane, the tmux server, both probes, jj/git/gh/tmux children of the runner, and the base of every gh child spawned for a GitHub App role (Task 2 threads it in place of process.env).
threeEnvironmentClasses.per-pane -e overlay (unchanged): processes.ts root/worker/controller env builders (LEGION_TREE/ISSUE/ROLE/WORKSPACE|ROOT_WORKSPACE/GENERATION/DAEMON_URL/PROJECT/STATE_DIR/CREDENTIAL_HELPER/CONTROL_SUBJECT/MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH/CONTROLLER, ENVOY_NATS_URL, ENVOY_URL, GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, PATH, DISPATCH_URL, DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE, and #992's credentialProcessEnvironment: worker-bin-first PATH, GH_CONFIG_DIR, empty GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_HOST, LEGION_GRANT_FILE) plus runtime-tmux.ts's `<SECRET>_FILE` pointer.
threeEnvironmentClasses.daemon-internal (process.env, keys allow: config.ts executePrivateKeyCommand (the one child that exists to read the App keys) and index/hotspots.ts's `jj log`. Nothing model-driven.

designSummary.stripFunctionFate: `stripDispatchEnv`/`PANE_SECRET_ENV_KEYS` are deleted. The spec's 'defensive second pass' is `isSecretLikeName` inside `paneEnvironment` and in github-app-env.ts's scrub; it is never the primary mechanism.
designSummary.supersedes992: #992 (merged 06:04Z) added LEGION_GRANT/LEGION_GRANT_FILE to the strip-list; under the allow-list no LEGION_* value is inherited at all, so those entries disappear with the list. #992's pathWithoutWorkerBin, installWorkerGhShim, and credentialProcessEnvironment are untouched.

groups.readers: HOME: OMP DirResolver (~/.omp), jj/git/gh user config, the `secrets` client ('HOME must be set to an absolute path' in its binary), envoy-client dispatch-config.ts:116. USER/LOGNAME: git/jj identity fallbacks. SHELL: tmux runs each pane's shell-command through `default-shell`, which tmux seeds from the server's $SHELL (production server: /bin/bash) - dropping it would switch panes to /bin/sh. TERM: named by acceptance 1; tmux also sets it per pane. LANG/LANGUAGE/LC_*: locale for every tool; LANG/LC_* are set on the production daemon.

TMPDIR: Bun os.tmpdir() in OMP and the legion CLI. TMUX_TMPDIR: where `tmux -L legion-<project>` looks for its socket (production daemon: /home/ubuntu/.tmux/sockets) - the daemon's own tmux commands run under paneEnv, so dropping it would make a restarted daemon look for the server under /tmp/tmux-<uid> and treat every live pane as gone. XDG_DATA_HOME/XDG_STATE_HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME/XDG_CACHE_HOME: OMP's DirResolver (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/omp` root), paths.ts:27-28, github-app-env.ts:10-11 (`legion gh` in a pane computes GH_CONFIG_DIR from XDG_STATE_HOME), and the smoke rig sets XDG_DATA_HOME/XDG_STATE_HOME on the daemon expecting panes to see the same scratch roots. XDG_RUNTIME_DIR: secretsd extension resolveRuntimeDir (secretsd.ts:109) and the `secrets` client's socket lookup.

OMP DirResolver profile root; boot-probes.ts:275-279 relies on the probe and the spawned panes resolving the same plugin root. Production sets OMP_PROFILE=legion both on the daemon and in omp_launch_prefix (`env OMP_PROFILE=legion secrets ... --`).

mise, for the daemon's own bootstrap `mise env --json` / `mise where <pin>` (now run under the allow-listed environment) and for the mise shims panes execute (`secrets`, `bun` are ~/.mise/shims/* -> mise). Verified 2026-09-13: `env -i HOME PATH mise where github:sjawhar/oh-my-pi@18.1.18-sami.20260912-203541` resolves to ~/.local/share/mise/installs/... while with MISE_DATA_DIR=$HOME/.mise (what ~/.dotfiles/.bashrc:36 exports and the production daemon carries) it resolves to ~/.mise/installs/... - a different binary. docs/solutions/legion/smoke-rig-modes-gate-checkpoints-and-the-pin-has-one-home.md records the same trap.

the `secrets` client and the secretsd OMP extension (`SECRETSD_SOCK`, else `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/secretsd.sock`, else /run/user/<uid>/secretsd.sock). A socket path, never a credential. NOT SECRETSD_SESSION_TOKEN_FILE - see excluded.
OMP/Bun (provider HTTP), gh, git, jj git push. None is set on this box; a deployment behind a proxy or a private CA would otherwise lose every provider and GitHub call silently.

the daemon's PATH is the input `mise env --json` extends; mise's PATH then replaces it in paneEnv (`resolveDaemonEnvironment` prepends <state_dir>/bin and strips worker-bin entries exactly as on main today).

allowList.rule: One name per line, grouped, each group's comment names the process that reads it. No prefix or wildcard entry. A pane that needs a variable not on the list is a bug in the list; the two start-up probes run under the same environment, so a variable OMP itself needs fails the boot loudly (spec Errors row) rather than the first pane.

excluded.why: the two App private keys; read only by config.ts executePrivateKeyCommand (daemon-internal). Present today on the production private tmux server (pid 2023008) and on every pane (e.g. worker pane 3193050) - names verified 2026-09-13, values never printed.
daemon config inputs; every pane already receives them explicitly from config as -e pairs (processes.ts root/worker/controller env builders). Inheritance would only mask a config bug.

listener/daemon-side secrets; no pane process needs them (ENVOY_TOKEN is read by envoy-client transport.ts:218 but is not set on this deployment; if a deployment ever needs it in panes it becomes an explicit per-pane export from config, never inheritance).
the bearer is startup config; panes get DISPATCH_URL + DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE as explicit -e pairs (processes.ts) - unchanged.

names: LEGION_* (every name: LEGION_TREE, LEGION_ISSUE, LEGION_ROLE, LEGION_WORKSPACE, LEGION_ROOT_WORKSPACE, LEGION_GENERATION, LEGION_DAEMON_URL, LEGION_PROJECT, LEGION_STATE_DIR, LEGION_CREDENTIAL_HELPER, LEGION_CONTROL_SUBJECT, LEGION_MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH, LEGION_CONTROLLER, LEGION_BOOT_TOKEN(_FILE), LEGION_CONTROLLER_SECRET(_FILE), LEGION_GRANT(_FILE), LEGION_OMP_PATH, LEGION_*_PATH, LEGION_DAEMON_PORT, ...)
excluded.why: per-pane values are set explicitly by processes.ts (-e pairs) and runtime-tmux.ts (*_FILE pointers); the rest are daemon config. A daemon started from inside a Legion pane inherits the outer pane's whole family - exactly the leak environment.ts's comment and #992 describe; the allow-list ends it wholesale, which supersedes #992's LEGION_GRANT/LEGION_GRANT_FILE strip entries.

provider credentials reach a pane only through omp_launch_prefix (`secrets ... -- omp`), resolved inside the pane; the daemon's own copies are the operator session's. Verified 2026-09-13 that `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$PATH USER=$USER secrets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -- sh -c '...'` injects the key with no tty and no session token, so probes and panes need nothing else from the daemon env for the prefix to work.
the operator OMP session's broker identity (its human-tier grants). Inheriting it binds every pane to the operator's secretsd session. Not needed: agent-tier keys resolve without it (verified above).
the operator session's id (LEGION-43); a pane's OMP must not believe it is that session's child.

the operator's outer tmux. The private server sets its own per pane; envoy-client dispatch-cwd.ts:134 targets `switch-client -t $TMUX_PANE`, so an inherited operator pane id is a mis-target. Same exclusion as packages/pi-envoy/scripts/grant-rig/run.ts:189.

on the production daemon it is `~/.config/jj/config.toml:~/.dotfiles/.jjconfig.toml:~/.cache/omp/jj/omp-attribution-<operator session>.toml` - the operator session's attribution overlay. jj finds the first two at its default user paths without JJ_CONFIG (verified: `env -i HOME PATH jj config path --user` -> ~/.jjconfig.toml (symlink to .dotfiles/.jjconfig.toml) and ~/.config/jj/config.toml); pi-envoy jj-attribution.ts appends the pane's own overlay either way.
the operator shell's gh-app routing gitconfig; panes set GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0 explicitly and get identity from the workspace's jj config and per-call buildRoleEnv.
the operator's SSH agent and session; repos are https with the Legion credential helper. Inheriting SSH_AUTH_SOCK hands panes the operator's SSH keys.
set per pane by processes.ts credentialProcessEnvironment (#992: empty GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_HOST, GH_CONFIG_DIR=<state_dir>/gh); never inherited.
mise shell-activation state of the operator shell; meaningless to a child and confusing to `mise env`.

names: everything else on the production daemon (MNEMOPI_*, CLAUDE_*, npm_*, NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX, NODE, STARSHIP_*, LS_COLORS, LESS*, BROWSER, AWSCLI_*, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, PULSE_SERVER, PCSCLITE_CSOCK_NAME, DOCKER_BUILDKIT, DEBUGINFOD_URLS, NCURSES_NO_UTF8_ACS, OPENCODE_GITHUB_REPO, XDG_DATA_DIRS, SHLVL, OLDPWD, PWD, _)
excluded.why: operator-shell state. Pane OMP configuration belongs to the legion profile (OMP_PROFILE=legion), not to the operator's session tuning. GOBIN/GOROOT/CARGO_HOME/RUSTUP_* still arrive when `mise env --json` emits them (it does on this box: AGENT_EVAL_VERSION, CARGO_HOME, GOBIN, GOROOT, PATH, RUSTUP_HOME, RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN).

evidenceGathered: Production private tmux server pid 2023008 (`tmux -L legion-sjawharlegion new-session -d ...`, parent systemd) carries 94 variables incl. GH_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64, GH_REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ENVOY_TAILSCALE_OAUTH_CLIENT_KEY, SECRETSD_SESSION_TOKEN_FILE, OMP_SESSION_ID, JJ_CONFIG (with the operator session's attribution overlay), GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 + KEY_0/VALUE_0, TMUX, TMUX_PANE, SSH_AUTH_SOCK, LEGION_OMP_PATH, MISE_DATA_DIR=~/.mise, TMUX_TMPDIR=~/.tmux/sockets, OMP_PROFILE=legion (names read from /proc; values never printed except the non-secret paths quoted). A live worker OMP pane (pid 3193050) carries every one of them plus the 14 `-e` pairs. The server env is frozen at fork time: the running daemon has since restarted with a different environment, which is why Task 7 exists.

`env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$PATH USER=$USER secrets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -- sh -c 'test -n "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" && echo present'` -> present, with no tty and no SECRETSD_SESSION_TOKEN_FILE: the launch prefix needs nothing from the daemon env beyond the allow-list.
`env -i HOME PATH mise where <omp pin>` -> ~/.local/share/mise/installs/... ; with MISE_DATA_DIR=$HOME/.mise -> ~/.mise/installs/... : MISE_DATA_DIR must be on the list.
`env -i HOME PATH jj config path --user` -> ~/.jjconfig.toml (-> .dotfiles/.jjconfig.toml) and ~/.config/jj/config.toml: jj needs no JJ_CONFIG here.
`mise env --json | jq keys` on this box: AGENT_EVAL_VERSION, CARGO_HOME, GOBIN, GOROOT, PATH, RUSTUP_HOME, RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN.

secretsd agent-tier keys (`secrets list`): ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GH_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64, GH_REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64, ENVOY_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET. DISPATCH_TOKEN is not one (LEGION-40).
CI triggers: pr-and-main.yaml runs on pull_request and push:main only - a pre-PR rebase costs no CI run.

Pane-side env readers inventoried (PaneEnvReadsScout, agent://PaneEnvReadsScout): pi-envoy legion.ts/classify.ts/envoy.ts, envoy-client defaults/dispatch-config/dispatch-cwd/machine/transport, legion CLI (LEGION_DAEMON_URL/PORT, LEGION_GRANT(_FILE), XDG_STATE_HOME, LEGION_*_PATH), secretsd extension + client (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, SECRETSD_SOCK, SECRETSD_SESSION_TOKEN_FILE, HOME), OMP binary strings (HOME, PATH, XDG_*, TMPDIR, OMP_PROFILE, PI_PROFILE, provider keys, proxies, SSL_CERT_*, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS).

steps: Replace AGENTS.md :111-123 with one paragraph (keep the DISPATCH_URL/DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE sentences that precede it): 'A pane's environment is built from an allow-list, never by stripping known secrets from the daemon's own. `resolveDaemonEnvironment` (`environment.ts`, `PANE_ENV_ALLOW_LIST` + `paneEnvironment`) copies exactly these daemon variables - HOME, USER, LOGNAME, SHELL, TERM, TZ, LANG, LANGUAGE, the thirteen LC_* names, TMPDIR, TMUX_TMPDIR, XDG_CACHE_HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, XDG_STATE_HOME, OMP_PROFILE, PI_PROFILE, MISE_CACHE_DIR, MISE_CONFIG_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR, MISE_STATE_DIR, SECRETSD_SOCK, HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY (both cases), SSL_CERT_DIR, SSL_CERT_FILE, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, and PATH (which `mise env` then replaces) - lays the complete `mise env --json` output over them, and drops any credential-shaped name (`isSecretLikeName`: `*_SECRET`, `*_TOKEN`, `*_GRANT`, `*_API_KEY`, `*_PASSWORD`, their `*_FILE` twins, and anything containing `PRIVATE_KEY`) as a second line of defence. That object is `paneEnv`: the environment of every command `createDaemonRunner` runs (jj, git, gh, tmux, both start-up probes), therefore of the private tmux server the first `tmux -L legion-<project>` command forks, therefore of every pane. On top of it a pane gets only the explicit `-e` pairs `processes.ts`/`runtime-tmux.ts` set (the LEGION_* family, ENVOY_NATS_URL/ENVOY_URL, GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, DISPATCH_URL/DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE, the credential pane environment below, and the `*_FILE` secret pointers). A `gh` child the daemon spawns for a GitHub App role (`buildRoleEnv`) starts from `paneEnv` too, minus GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_HOST/GH_CONFIG_DIR/LEGION_GITHUB_APP_* and credential-shaped names, plus the minted GH_TOKEN, GH_CONFIG_DIR and GIT_* identity. A pane that needs a variable not on the list is a bug in the list (add the name with its reader in the group comment), never a wildcard; the daemon's own start-up probes run under the same environment, so a missing variable OMP itself needs fails the boot loudly instead of the first pane.'

tasks.title: Pull request, handoff, and the post-release steps (acceptance 3, 4, 5)
steps: Push and open the PR per the legion-worker skill: `jj bookmark set legion/LEGION-74 && jj git push --bookmark legion/LEGION-74`; `legion gh -- pr create --title 'fix(daemon): panes, probes, and daemon children inherit an allow-listed environment, never the GitHub App keys (LEGION-74)' --body-file <file>`. Body: `Dispatch: LEGION-74`; Summary in plain words (the keys were readable by every pane; now a pane gets only a named list); the READY-format Verification block (CI / Threads / Thermo / E2E / Fast-follow: none / Chain: not stacked); a **Deployment (operator, in this order)** section: 1. `legion stop sjawhar-legion`; 2. `tmux -L legion-sjawharlegion kill-server` (the server keeps its fork-time environment across daemon restarts - the old one still carries both keys; every pane dies and comes back by `--resume`; pick a quiet moment); 3. start the daemon on the merged main through the same `secrets GH_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64 GH_REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64 -- ...` launcher (the daemon still needs the keys for its own token minting); 4. the boot log must NOT show the `carries N environment variable(s)` warning (Task 7); 5. tell the implementer (this issue) so it runs the production check below. Tier for the merger's READY packet: T1 (deploy correctness / live credential exposure), stated with the reason.

`.legion/implement.json`: filesChanged, trickyParts (the #992 start point; gh children's base env; TMUX_TMPDIR/MISE_DATA_DIR/SHELL findings; the stale-server fact), `smokeProof` (Task 6 quotes), `deployment` (the operator steps above), `postRelease` (the checklist below, unticked). Commit `implement: record handoff`, push.

POST-RELEASE (acceptance 3 and 4; you are resumed for it): after the operator relaunches - (a) `pid=$(tmux -L legion-sjawharlegion display-message -p '#{pid}')` must differ from 2023008 and `tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/$pid/environ | grep -c PRIVATE_KEY` -> 0; (b) controller pane: `tmux -L legion-sjawharlegion list-panes -a -F '#{window_name} #{pane_id} #{pane_pid}' | awk '$1=="controller"'` -> `tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/<pid>/environ | grep -c PRIVATE_KEY` -> 0; (c) one worker pane spawned after the relaunch (`legion state` -> a role whose `readyConfirmedAt` is later than the relaunch) -> 0; (d) acceptance 4: from that fresh worker (ask its architect, or use your own next `legion gh` call once you are respawned): `legion gh -- api repos/sjawhar/legion --jq .full_name` -> `sjawhar/legion` with a 200 in the daemon log - a live grant minted from the keys the daemon alone holds. Quote (a)-(d) as a PR comment with the Legion footer (the spec says 'quoted in the pull request') and in a `dispatch_message` on LEGION-74.

ROTATION MESSAGE (acceptance 5; a plain `dispatch_message` to Sami on LEGION-74 - never an ask; deployment rule 2026-09-12): 'Both GitHub App private keys (implementer App 3202636, reviewer App 3202653) have been readable by every Legion pane since the deployment started; the fix is live and a fresh pane now shows neither. Current state: the keys are still the exposed ones. Desired state: new keys, old ones revoked. Proposed change: in GitHub (Settings -> Developer settings -> GitHub Apps -> app -> Private keys) generate a new key for each app, base64-encode each .pem (`base64 -w0 key.pem`), store them as the secretsd agent-tier keys GH_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64 and GH_REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64 (`secrets edit`), have the operator relaunch the daemon (its launcher already injects both through `secrets ... --`), then delete the old keys on the same GitHub pages. Options: rotate at the next relaunch (recommended - one restart, no extra pane churn) or rotate now (a second relaunch today). I will verify afterwards by minting a grant from a fresh worker (`legion gh` returning 200) and record it here.' Then, once the operator records the rotation on this issue, do that verification and record the result (no key material anywhere).

acceptanceMap.1: Task 1 TEST A (environment.test.ts, the spec's scenario) + Task 2 (gh children)
acceptanceMap.3: Task 8 post-release check; Task 7 warning; Task 5 AGENTS.md re-fork note; Task 6 checkpoint 13 is the same shape on the rig
acceptanceMap.4: Task 3 (private_key_command keeps process.env) + existing github-apps/config tests + Task 8 (d) live grant
acceptanceMap.5: Task 8 rotation message + post-rotation grant check
acceptanceMap.7: Task 6 proof run (implementer) repeated by the tester

concerns: Start point: this workspace is at 19b99c3c, main@origin is #992 + release chores ahead, and #992 edits the exact hunks this change rewrites. Task 0 starts the branch on main@origin before any commit or PR exists (zero CI cost, verified against the workflow triggers) rather than opening a PR that GitHub reports CONFLICTING on arrival. Architect: this is my reading of the 2026-09-11 rule's rationale; say so if you want the letter followed instead (write against 19b99c3c, rebase when CONFLICTING).

Production is not fixed by the daemon restart alone: the private tmux server keeps its fork-time environment (it still has both keys today although the daemon has restarted since). The operator relaunch must `tmux -L legion-sjawharlegion kill-server` between stop and start - every live pane dies and resumes by design. Task 8's Deployment section, Task 5's AGENTS.md note, and Task 7's boot warning carry this; acceptance 3 fails without it.

Task 7 is scope the spec did not ask for (a ~40-line boot warning). It exists because the invariant is otherwise unenforced across the daemon's normal restart path. Separable commit; cut it by telling the implementer.

The `mise env --json` output is allowed wholesale (acceptance 1 says so). A mise.toml `[env]` entry the operator adds reaches panes unless its name is credential-shaped - by design; the daemon cannot know which operator toolchain variables OMP needs.

Excluding JJ_CONFIG, SSH_AUTH_SOCK, TMUX/TMUX_PANE, OMP_SESSION_ID, GIT_CONFIG_* and the operator's MNEMOPI_*/CLAUDE_* is a behaviour change for panes (they inherited them until now). Each is the operator session's state, not deployment config; jj/git/mise/tmux were verified to work without them on this box. If the rig run in Task 6 shows a pane that does not boot, the missing name goes on the list with its reader - never a wildcard.

The proof run needs the shared smoke rig (envoy mode: production NATS bridge + LEGSMOKE Dispatch project + sjawhar/legion-smoke) and real model turns for the root architect to reach a worker pane: budget 30-60 minutes of wall time and run it in the background while writing docs and the PR body. One rig per box at a time is the LEGION-41 limitation; up.sh reuses an existing legion-smoke-nats container on the same port.

Tests deleted, not re-pinned: config.test.ts:890 (private_key_command strip) and environment.test.ts:157/:277 (strip-list assertions, replaced by the exact-equality allow-list tests); github-apps.test.ts:603's DISPATCH_URL/DISPATCH_MCP_URL assertions (a URL is not a credential).
